company_verdict: Accenture is one of the highest-value targets on his list, but NOTHING on this Workday board is for him. All 20 postings are AIOC (Accenture India Operations Centre) BPO delivery seats — "Any Graduation", "1 to 3 years", "may require you to work in rotational shifts", and an immediate start. Not one mentions SQL, Python, Power BI, EDA, forecasting models, business analysis or consulting; the closest any gets is "Prepare basic reports, trackers and dashboards" in an LMS-admin req. The file itself states campus/fresher hiring is NOT in this feed and runs through college placement cells. So: apply to Accenture aggressively — through the DJSCE TPO and the off-campus 2027-batch fresher drive, aimed at Data & AI / Advanced App Engineering — and ignore this board entirely.
best_channel: CAMPUS (DJSCE placement cell), with a final-sem internship as the fallback. Justification, in the research's own words: student_programs says "NOT IN THIS FEED — Accenture India campus/fresher hiring runs through its own off-campus drives and college placement cells, not this Workday board. Screening agent should treat DJSCE campus placement as the primary channel." DJSCE is a target school for Accenture's Mumbai hiring and Accenture is a volume recruiter there — his 8.82 CGPA, zero backlogs and CSE-Data Science specialisation clear every campus cut-off Accenture sets (they typically gate at 60%/6.0 CGPA, so he is far above the line and eligible for the higher "Advanced" / Data & AI band rather than the base ASE band). Referral-only and off-cycle experienced reqs are both dead ends here: the AIOC reqs on this board are screened on years-of-experience and rotational-shift availability, not pedigree, so no referral rescues a May-2027 grad against a "1 to 3 years" bar.
may_2027_fit: Fatal mismatch with this feed, excellent fit with the channel that isn't in it. (1) Every posting here — including the two lowest-bar ones, Learning Operations New Associate AIOC-S01667495 and HR Service Delivery New Associate AIOC-S01667460, both "Years of Experience: 0 to 1 years" — is a live AIOC delivery req posted 22-24 Sep 2026 that backfills a seat now. AIOC reqs close in 2-6 weeks. He cannot start full-time before ~June 2027, which is 8-9 months out; the requisition will not be held. Applying converts him into a rejected-candidate record in Accenture's Workday, which is a real cost when the campus team later pulls his profile. Do not apply. (2) The date that actually matters: Accenture's campus process for the June/July-2027 joining batch runs roughly Aug 2026 – Jan 2027 at Mumbai engineering colleges, and its large off-campus 2027-batch fresher drive historically opens Sep–Nov 2026. That window is OPEN RIGHT NOW (today is 24 Sep 2026). Action this week: register with the DJSCE TPO for the Accenture 2027 slot, confirm which band he is eligible for (base ASE vs. the higher Advanced App Engineering / Data & AI band — he should push for the latter on CGPA + DS specialisation), and set up a job alert on accenture.com/in-en/careers for "Full Stack Engineering Analyst"/"Data & AI" 2027-batch postings. (3) Declared availability wherever he does apply: "Available full-time from 1 June 2027; available for a full-time internship from January 2027 to May 2027." (4) The Jan–May 2027 final-sem internship is NOT servable by anything in this feed — Accenture India does not run a structured final-semester internship on this Workday board, so spend that slot on a fintech/analytics firm or a consulting boutique instead and use Accenture's campus offer as the full-time anchor.
referral_strategy: Split the referral effort by channel, because leverage is wildly different. (A) ZERO leverage — the 20 AIOC reqs on this board (AIOC-S016675xx / S016672xx / S016671xx). These are screened by an operations recruiting pod on years-of-experience, qualification string ("BCom" for Record to Report AIOC-S01667572) and shift availability. A referral does not move an employee-referral bonus past a "1 to 3 years" / immediate-joiner gate. Burning a referral here wastes it. (B) HIGH leverage — DJSCE alumni inside Accenture for the 2027 campus batch and for Accenture Data & AI / Strategy & Consulting. Concretely: (1) LinkedIn > DJSCE alumni page > filter "Current company: Accenture" > "Mumbai" — DJSCE has a large Accenture alumni base; message 2019-2024 graduating batches who are now Analyst/Consultant/Data Science Analyst, not Associates. Script: "DJSCE CSE-DS, 2027 batch, 8.82. Our Accenture campus slot is coming up — are you in Data & AI or S&C? Would value 10 mins on which band to target and whether I should flag the DS specialisation to the TPO." (2) The DJSCE TPO / placement coordinators are a stronger lever than any individual referrer for the campus channel — get in front of them first, this week. (3) Accenture India campus recruiters on LinkedIn (search "Accenture" + "Campus Recruitment" / "Early Careers" + India) — connect with a note naming DJSCE and the 2027 batch; do not pitch the AIOC reqs to them. (4) His Infiheal Founder's Office network — anyone who worked the IndiGo or HDFC Bank pipeline may know Accenture partners on the client side; a partner-level intro into Accenture Strategy & Consulting is worth more than ten analyst referrals, and his "Ace The Case" IIT Bombay 4th-of-400 (post-merger workforce restructuring, +22.4% output-to-cost) is the exact artefact to lead with in that conversation.

skills_to_learn.skill: Advanced Excel + PowerPoint reporting (pivot tables, Power Query, INDEX/MATCH + XLOOKUP, slicer-driven trackers, clean deck-ready charts)
skills_to_learn.why: Highest openings-unlocked count on this board: named verbatim in 5 postings — "Proficient in Excel, PowerPoint and Word" (Recruiting Associate AIOC-S01667523, -524, -525), "Proficiency in MS Office tools including Excel, Word and Outlook" (Learning Operations New Associate AIOC-S01667495), "Proficiency in MS Office Excel, Word, PowerPoint for tracking, reporting, and documentation" (HR Service Delivery New Associate AIOC-S01667460) — plus the reporting duties "Prepare basic reports, trackers and dashboards related to training activities" and "Generate recruitment reports and dashboards as needed". It is also the one skill here that survives outside Accenture: every BA/BI/analyst JD in India tests Excel, and his profile currently shows pandas/PowerBI but no explicit advanced-Excel line. He does Series A investor decks at Infiheal, so the PowerPoint half is already there — close the Excel half and put "Advanced Excel (Power Query, pivots, dynamic dashboards)" on the resume.
skills_to_learn.resource: Microsoft Learn "Excel" + "Get & Transform (Power Query)" modules; ExcelJet formula reference; Leila Gharani / ExcelIsFun Power Query and pivot playlists. Build one deliverable: rebuild his freelance registration-platform funnel drop-off data as a Power Query -> pivot -> slicer dashboard so he can demo it in an interview.

skills_to_learn.skill: Demand planning & replenishment fundamentals (forecast accuracy MAPE/WMAPE, safety stock, reorder point, ABC/XYZ segmentation, S&OP basics)
skills_to_learn.why: Unlocks 2 postings by their named primary skill: "Primary skill - Retail Forecasting & Replenishment - P1" (Supply Chain Operations Associate AIOC-S01667628) and "Skill required: Fulfill - Fulfillment Operations" with "Generate client required reports and agreed frequencies" (Supply Chain Operations Associate AIOC-S01667107). Recommended not for those reqs — he can't start in time — but because supply-chain analytics is a genuine analyst track at Accenture Operations and Data & AI, and it is the only domain on this whole board that plugs directly into what he already has: pandas/NumPy/scikit-learn time-series work and the CypherSOL automation pipelines. Learning the vocabulary converts his existing ML skills into a named Accenture capability he can claim in a campus interview.
skills_to_learn.resource: Coursera Rutgers "Supply Chain Analytics" (audit free); Nicolas Vandeput's "Data Science for Supply Chain Forecasting" intro chapters + his open forecasting notebooks. Deliverable: a Python notebook forecasting a public retail dataset (M5 or Kaggle store-sales) reporting WMAPE and a reorder-point calc.

skills_to_learn.skill: ITIL 4 Foundation (incident vs. problem management, root-cause, SLA discipline)
skills_to_learn.why: Unlocks 3 postings by their named primary skill: "Primary skill - Problem Management - P3" with "Manage problems caused by information technology infrastructure errors ... by seeking the root cause of those incidents and initiating actions to improve or correct the situation" (Network & Svcs Operation Associate AIOC-S01667290, -291, -292). Honest caveat: these are Navi Mumbai rotational-shift billing-ops seats and are a bad career fit for him. The certificate is worth it only as a low-cost credential line that also reads well for service-delivery/ops-analyst and product-operations roles — one of his stated wants. Rank it third; skip it if time is tight.
skills_to_learn.effort: 2-3 weeks self-study; exam fee ~INR 25-30k (paid). Only do this if someone else is paying or a specific JD demands it.
skills_to_learn.resource: AXELOS ITIL 4 Foundation official study guide; free syllabus summaries on the PeopleCert site. Do NOT pay for a bootcamp.

skills_to_learn.skill: Workday Recruiting module + ATS fundamentals (Smart Recruiter, requisition/pipeline data hygiene)
skills_to_learn.why: Second-highest raw count — named in 4 postings: "Knowledge of Workday Recruiting module" (Recruiting Associate AIOC-S01667523, -524, -525) and "Primary skill - Workday Recruiting" / "Working knowledge of Applicant Tracking Systems ATS, Smart Recruiter" (HR Service Delivery New Associate AIOC-S01667460). Listed for completeness and then explicitly DE-recommended: this is a closed-loop HR-ops tool skill with near-zero transfer into business analyst, BI, analytics, risk or strategy work, and the reqs it unlocks also demand Australian-shift availability ("Must be open to Australian shift timings, 9 am to 5 pm Australian time"). For a DJSCE CSE-Data Science final-year with 13x case-competition podiums, learning Workday Recruiting to chase an AIOC associate seat is a downgrade. Do not spend the 2 weeks.
skills_to_learn.effort: 1-2 weeks if he ignored this advice. Recommendation: 0 weeks — skip.

skills_to_learn.skill: Financial accounting fundamentals (balance sheet account reconciliation, sub-ledger vs. GL, IFRS/Ind-AS basics)
skills_to_learn.why: Unlocks 2 postings: "Primary skill - Balance Sheet Account Reconciliations - P3" (Record to Report Ops Associate AIOC-S01667572) and "Primary skill - Accounting & Financial Reporting Standards - P3" (Record to Report Ops Associate AIOC-S01667404). Lowest priority of the five and effectively blocked: AIOC-S01667572 hard-gates on "Qualifications: BCom", which his B.Tech does not satisfy, and for AIOC-S01667404 he would be competing against BCom/CA-Inter candidates who have done recon work for real. The only reason to touch this is that his Computational Finance coursework and the CypherSOL bank-statement work already brush against it, and basic accounting literacy helps in risk-analytics and fintech BA interviews — which is a different, better goal than these two reqs.
skills_to_learn.effort: 3-4 weeks if targeting fintech/risk BA interviews generally; do not do it for these two reqs.
skills_to_learn.resource: NPTEL/Coursera "Financial Accounting Fundamentals" (UVA Darden, audit free); Corporate Finance Institute free accounting track.
